name: Rowing Machine Intervals — Ergometer
description: Rowing machine intervals on an ergometer produce one of the highest whole-body cardiovascular demands available in a gym setting, engaging approximately 86% of skeletal muscle mass in each stroke. Each rowing stroke follows a sequence of leg drive, body swing, and arm pull, distributing load across the quadriceps, gluteus maximus, latissimus dorsi, rhomboids, and biceps simultaneously. The absence of eccentric ground-reaction forces makes the rower extremely joint-friendly while generating a metabolic demand comparable to running sprints.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the seat with feet strapped securely in the footrests. Grip the handle with an overhand grip, arms extended, shins vertical, and body hinged slightly forward with a neutral spine (the 'catch' position).
execution.setup_instructions: Set the damper (resistance lever) to 4–6 for most training. Higher damper settings feel heavier but are not necessarily better — elite rowers often train at 3–5. Connect the performance monitor and set the target for distance or time.
steps: Step 1: Begin at the catch — shins vertical, arms straight, body leaning slightly forward with a flat back.
Step 2: Drive: push through both legs forcefully, keeping the arms straight until the legs are nearly extended.
Step 3: Swing: once the legs are 90% extended, swing the torso back to 1 o'clock (slightly past vertical) using the hips.
Step 4: Pull: once the body is swung back, draw the handle into the lower sternum by bending the elbows and pulling the shoulder blades together.
Step 5: Recover: extend the arms first, then hinge the torso forward, then bend the knees and slide forward to the catch. Maintain a 2:1 recovery-to-drive ratio in time.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at the beginning of the drive phase. Inhale on the recovery as you slide forward. Maintain a consistent breathing rhythm matched to the stroke rate.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms before the legs have driven — the sequence must always be legs, body, arms
Rounding the lower back at the catch, which places the spine under shear load
Jerking the handle rather than maintaining a smooth, connected drive
safety_considerations: Establish proper technique at a moderate intensity before attempting sprint intervals
Avoid excessive layback past 1 o'clock, which compresses the lumbar spine under load
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full leg drive from a compressed position to nearly locked-out. Handle should travel from full arm extension to touching the sternum just below the pectoral muscles.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Interval option: 500m hard / 2 minutes easy × 6–8 rounds. Tabata option: 20 seconds maximum effort / 10 seconds rest × 8. Stroke rate during sprint: 28–34 SPM.
coaching_cues: Legs, body, arms — arms, body, legs. That is the entire stroke
Push the foot plate away, do not pull the handle
Hang your body weight off the handle at the catch
